meta.title: Snapchat Video Length Limit: 60 Seconds per Snap, 5–60 s for Web Stories (2026) | {{SITE_NAME}}
meta.description: Snapchat videos are limited to 60 seconds; Story uploads from the web must be 5 to 60 seconds and 9:16. The file can be around 1 GB, so length is the limit you hit. Trim your video to the exact seconds in your browser — nothing uploaded.
og.title: Snapchat video length limit: 60 seconds
og.description: 60 seconds per Snap, 5–60 s for web Stories, ~1 GB files. Trim to the exact second in your browser.
hero.title: Snapchat video length limit
hero.lead: Snapchat limits videos by time, not size: 60 seconds per Snap, and Story uploads from the web must be between 5 and 60 seconds in a vertical 9:16 frame. Snapchat publishes no file-size figure — about 1 GB is the practical ceiling — so the only thing that stops a phone recording is being too long.
qa.h2: Snapchat video limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: Length. Phone recordings almost never reach 1 GB, but anything over 60 seconds has to be cut down before it can be a single Snap.
qa.after: Snapchat also recompresses every video it receives, so the file size you upload has little effect on what your friends see. Getting the clip to the right 60 seconds is the edit that matters — and choosing which 60 beats letting the app decide.
tool.lead: Drop the video below and drag the start and end handles over the preview until the line underneath reads 60 seconds or less. The cut is exact to a tenth of a second and the result is a standard MP4, made on your own device — nothing is uploaded until you post it yourself.
fit.h2: How long can a Snapchat video be?
fit.caption: Snapchat video length limits
fit.r3.q: Trim to the 60 seconds you want before uploading
fit.r4.q: About 1 GB, unofficial — not the limit you'll hit
fit.after: Snapchat's help pages don't publish a file-size figure, so the 1 GB is best available information; the durations are the ones the app enforces. The date these were last verified is at the top of this page.
over.h2: Over 60 seconds? Cut it, don't shrink it
over.p1: Compressing a Snapchat video changes nothing about its length, and Snapchat recompresses it again on upload anyway. Trim instead: pick the moment, cut it to 60 seconds or less, and post that. For a longer story, cut it into several Snaps of up to a minute each and post them in order.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark. If you also need the file smaller for some other reason, the compressor keeps the picture sharp while shrinking it.
faq.q1: How long can a Snapchat video be?
faq.a1: 60 seconds per Snap. Story uploads from the web must be between 5 and 60 seconds and vertical (9:16).
faq.q2: Is there a file size limit on Snapchat?
faq.a2: Snapchat doesn't publish one; around 1 GB is the practical ceiling. Phone recordings almost never reach it, so length is the limit that matters.
faq.q3: Can I post a video longer than 60 seconds?
faq.a3: Not as a single Snap. Trim it to the part you want, or cut a longer video into several clips of up to 60 seconds and post them one after another to your Story.
faq.a4: Hardly any — the kept range is re-encoded at a high setting, and Snapchat recompresses the upload to its own settings regardless. The cut lands exactly where you place the handles, not at the nearest keyframe.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I trim it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is where you post or send it yourself.
